title: Coastal & Mangrove Restoration
keywords_for_the_page_and_card: Blue carbon · Mangrove ecology · Sediment accretion · Community science
intro: Mangrove forests protect coastlines, store carbon and support fisheries. We measure whether restoration actually restores those functions — and at what pace.

add_focus_list: Sediment-trap monitoring of accretion and carbon burial
Community-run nurseries in three Southeast Asian estuaries
Post-restoration recovery of fish and invertebrate communities
add_paragraph:
Coastal restoration is often measured in hectares planted. We measure what those hectares do: how fast sediment accumulates, how much organic carbon it buries, and whether the nursery-reared seedlings survive their first two monsoon seasons.

Our pilot began in 2021 with one estuary and now spans three, with 120,000 propagules raised annually by community cooperatives. Every site is monitored with the same sediment-trap protocol so the numbers can be compared.
